name: github
title: GitHub
description: Mints a GitHub App installation token for the repositories a run works on, with the permissions the machine allows and no more.

app_id.title: App id
app_id.description: The GitHub App's numeric id, or its client id.

installation_id.title: Installation id
installation_id.description: The App's installation on the account whose repositories runs work on. Absent means it is looked up from the repositories on every call.

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.description: The most a run's token gets, by GitHub's permission name, of those a run may be granted: read or write, never admin. At least one; absent is the default. Administration, secrets, environments and every organisation's and member's permission are refused. workflows write lets a run change the repositories' workflows, which run with their Actions secrets, so grant it only to runs that must edit workflows. An App that qory-github setup creates lacks it until its owner adds it on GitHub.

api_url.title: API
api_url.description: GitHub's API, where qory-github sends the App's token: https://api.github.com, the default, or http or https on a loopback host, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1 or localhost, for a test. GitHub Enterprise Server is not supported.

private_key_file.title: Private key file
private_key_file.description: A file that contains the App's private key and that only its owner reads: the one way to hand the key in on a command line.

private_key.title: Private key
private_key.description: The App's private key, the PEM GitHub hands out. Secret: written, never read back, and never on a command line.

source.description: Brings in the tickets of the repositories an organisation installs the GitHub App on.

setup.help: Click Set up in Qory Apiary to open the server's setup page. Enter the GitHub account for the App, an organisation or a user. GitHub then opens with the App filled in, named qory- and that account's handle, which you can change. The server stores the App's keys in Qory Apiary.

source.connect: Install takes you to GitHub. There you choose the account to install it on, and whether it reaches all of that account's repositories or only those you select.
source.access: These are the repositories GitHub lets this installation reach. To add or remove one, change the installation's repository access on GitHub.
source.disconnect: To uninstall GitHub, remove its installation on GitHub.

setup.before: Sign in to GitHub first, as the user you create the App for, or as an owner of the organisation you create it for.
steps: The page Set up the GitHub App opens. In GitHub account for the App, enter the organisation or user to create the App for, such as example-org.
Under Who can install the App, keep Only this account (private), or choose Any GitHub account (public) if other GitHub accounts must install the App.
Press Continue. GitHub opens with the App filled in, named qory-example-org; you can change the name there.
On GitHub, press Create GitHub App.
When the page shows that the GitHub App is set up, click Back to Qory Apiary.

connect.before: You need to be the GitHub user whose repositories you connect, or an owner of the organisation they belong to.
steps: If GitHub shows its sign-in page, sign in.
If GitHub shows a page to authorise the App, press Authorize.
If GitHub shows a list of accounts, choose the account to install the App on, such as example-org.
Choose All repositories, or choose Only select repositories and pick the repositories to bring in.
Press Install. GitHub then sends you back to Qory Apiary.
connect.after: If a page shows The App is already installed, press Continue on GitHub, choose the account, then press Save.
